finding.claim: The /logo handler fetches an attacker-supplied URL whose only validation is a substring check for 'example.io', so arbitrary internal or external hosts can be reached and the full response is returned to the caller.
finding.sink: http.Get(raw) at main.go:36, with the response body copied to the client at main.go:38

trace.note: raw := r.FormValue("logo"); attacker-controlled query or form value, no normalization
strings.Contains(raw, "example.io") is the only check; it matches anywhere in the string, including query, fragment, or userinfo
http.Get(raw) uses the default client, follows up to 10 redirects, and accepts any http/https URL
io.Copy(w, resp.Body) streams the upstream response back to the requester (non-blind SSRF)

finding.guards_checked: Substring check at main.go:32 is bypassable (e.g. http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/?example.io, http://127.0.0.1:8080/admin#example.io, http://attacker.com/?example.io). No scheme allowlist beyond net/http's http/https (plain HTTP to internal IPs and ports still reachable). No redirect validation. No private/loopback/link-local IP blocking, no port restriction.

verdict.guard_found: none. The only check is strings.Contains(raw, "example.io") at main.go:32, a substring match that does not close the finding. The `trusted` hostname map and `noRedirect` at main.go:10-12 are used only by the /cdn handler (main.go:20-24), not by /logo.
verdict.reason: The value comes from r.FormValue("logo") at main.go:31 with no auth, and main.go:32 accepts any string containing "example.io", so http.Get(raw) at main.go:36 reaches attacker-chosen hosts and io.Copy at main.go:38 returns the response body to the requester.
